title: FrugalGPT gateway cascade fronting spec-accelerated target pool
claimMd: An API gateway that runs a learned FrugalGPT-style LLM cascade (small model first, escalate to large only when a generation scorer is below threshold) in front of a vLLM target pool configured with MTP/EAGLE + chunked prefill beats monolithic always-70B vLLM on $/token by an ESTIMATE 2–4× for enterprise chat mixes where ≥40% of queries are answerable by a 7B-class model at matched task quality. Mechanism: FrugalGPT reports up to 98% inference cost reduction vs always using the best API model on HEADLINES while matching accuracy; the remaining hard fraction pays fewer decode forwards per token via speculation on the large pool. Quality gate: cascade must be trained/ calibrated on the customer’s label distribution—not zero-shot routing.
evidenceMd:
FrugalGPT cascade cost/accuracy: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.05176 (up to 98% cost reduction vs best single model; +4% accuracy at same cost on some benchmarks).

FrugalGPT implementation reference: https://github.com/stanford-futuredata/frugalgpt

vLLM MTP (no separate draft, shared KV): https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features/speculative_decoding/mtp/

Orchestrator default workload 512/128 chat in ledger.

Survey: survey/batching-speculative.md. Cost range ESTIMATE; assumes self-hosted 7B+70B fleet with router overhead ≪ model forward cost.

title: Heterogeneous P/D: H100 prefill + A100 decode pools
claimMd: For SLO-constrained chat serving (512 prompt / 128 completion tokens) on Llama-class 8B–70B models, Splitwise-style heterogeneous disaggregation (compute-heavy prefill on H100, memory-bound decode on cheaper A100 or power-capped GPUs) reduces cloud $/token by an ESTIMATED 25–45% versus a homogeneous monolithic vLLM fleet at equal throughput and tail latency, because decode does not need latest-gen FLOPs but colocated continuous batching forces a single expensive SKU.
evidenceMd: Splitwise (ISCA 2024) reports up to 1.4× higher throughput at ~20% lower cost on production Azure traces, and Splitwise-HA (H100 prompt + A100 token) capitalizes on lower Perf/$ for memory-bound decode (Insight VII; Fig 8–9 power capping). Token phase often runs batch ≤20 active tokens 60–70% of time on conversational traces, leaving compute idle on monolithic H100. Fair baseline: vLLM continuous batching on uniform H100. Costs: duplicate weights + IB KV transfer (~64–160 MiB per 512-token request for 8B/70B at 128–320 KiB/token per https://blog.prompt20.com/posts/kv-cache/ ). Regime failure: cross-AZ networks where KV egress $ dominates.

title: SLO-goodput P/D beats vLLM parallelism tuning alone
claimMd: Under strict TTFT+TPOT attainment (≥90%), DistServe-class prefill/decode disaggregation with bandwidth-aware KV placement yields 1.5–4× higher request goodput per GPU-hour than monolithic vLLM with continuous batching (even with optimized intra-op parallelism), translating to an ESTIMATED 30–75% lower $/token once weight duplication is accounted for—largest on 512+ token prompts and mixed chat traces; gains shrink to <15% for short prompts or loose SLOs where chunked prefill suffices.
evidenceMd: DistServe (OSDI 2024) vs vLLM baseline: 2.0–7.4× request rate on ShareGPT; 4.3× rate / 12.6× tighter SLO on LongBench summarization (OPT-66B); colocated goodput ~1.6 rps/GPU vs isolated phases on 13B/512/64 (Fig 1). vLLM++ parallelism search matched default vLLM—disaggregation required for goodput lift (§6.3). KV transfer overhead manageable with NVLink colocation or ~800G IB; OPT-66B 512-token KV ~1.13GB, 10 rps needs ~90Gbps to hide transfer (§3.3). TetriInfer reports 38% fewer resources vs colocated baseline (arXiv:2401.11181). Mooncake production: +75% requests with P/D + KV-centric scheduling (arXiv:2407.00079). Artifact: survey/disaggregated-serving.md

title: Composite hosting: heterogeneous P/D + LMCache/NIXL + FP8 decode pool
claimMd: A production-shaped hosting topology—(1) Splitwise-style heterogeneous fleet (H100-class prefill pool, A100-class decode pool with FP8-resident KV), (2) vLLM/LMCache MultiConnector P/D handoff (NixlConnector) plus optional LMCacheMP prefix tier with py-kvcache-style break-even admission (load external KV only when prefix_len ≥ L*)—beats well-tuned monolithic vLLM* (continuous batch + PagedAttention + tuned chunked prefill + FP8 + APC) on $/token by an ESTIMATED 1.6–2.5× for orchestrator-default 512/128 chat under strict tail-ITL SLOs, and by an ESTIMATED 2–4× when prefix hit rate h≥20% on shared system/multi-turn traffic. Mechanism: P/D removes phase interference and right-sizes SKUs; FP8 expands decode batch on cheap GPUs; gated LMCache avoids paying I/O on cold 512-token unique prompts but captures Mooncake-class reuse when h is material.
evidenceMd: Splitwise: 1.4× throughput @ ~20% lower cost (heterogeneous pools): https://arxiv.org/pdf/2311.18677.pdf. DistServe: 2–7.4× goodput vs vLLM under SLOs (disagg value): https://arxiv.org/html/2401.09670v3. Mooncake P/D + disaggregated KV (+75% prod requests): https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.00079. LMCache MultiConnector (NIXL handoff + MP reuse): https://docs.lmcache.ai/mp/disaggregated_prefill.html. py-kvcache break-even gating: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11744. FP8 KV concurrency on decode: https://vllm-project.github.io/2026/04/22/fp8-kvcache.html. Sarathi-Serve 2.6× vs vLLM sets vLLM* baseline bar: https://www.usenix.org/conference/osdi24/presentation/agrawal. PD agg vs disagg SLO regimes: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.01989v1. Artifact: survey/disagg-composition-and-baseline.md. All $/token multipliers ESTIMATE.

title: Scale-to-zero vLLM* burst pool beats always-on monolith at low avg utilization
claimMd: For mixed chat (512/128) where sustained goodput keeps GPUs active ≪100% of wall time (peak:avg GPU demand ~5–10×+, typical of spiky B2B APIs), an outer hosting layer—(1) right-sized **reserved** vLLM* on cheaper SKUs (L40S/A100 FP8) for baseline load, (2) **per-second scale-to-zero** overflow on the same engine (Modal/Replicate-class)—lowers **$/token** versus a monolithic always-on 4×H100 vLLM* fleet at equal SLO, because effective `C_hour` tracks **billed GPU-seconds** not `G×N×3600`. This does **not** beat a **fully utilized** vLLM* fleet at the rubric’s λ≈400 rps anchor; it beats **over-provisioned** GPU hosting that the rubric’s 85% util baseline already assumes away.
evidenceMd: **Utilization economics:** Modal documents serverless GPU win vs reservations when peak:avg ≈5–10× ([Modal blog](https://modal.com/blog/how-to-price-serverless)); scale-to-zero avoids idle charges ([Modal pricing](https://modal.com/pricing)). **Same engine:** Serverless runs user vLLM/SGLang containers—not a CPU substitute. **SKU ladder:** Modal L40S ~$1.95/hr vs H100 ~$3.95/hr vs EC2 H100 ~$12/hr ([Modal pricing](https://modal.com/pricing), rubric AWS ref). **Low-λ penalty on dedicated GPU:** At λ=10 rps, tokens/hr = 10×640×3600 = 23M; one always-on H100 at $12/hr → ~$0.52/1M tokens if fully allocated—but real fleets keep N GPUs 24×7 while active fraction ≪1, inflating $/token (ESTIMATE algebra from rubric §2). **CPU/edge refuted** for this mission: llama.cpp ~20 tok/s vs GPU vLLM 10³+ tok/s class ([EPYC 7282 bench](https://ahelpme.com/ai/llm-inference-benchmarks-with-llamacpp-and-amd-epyc-7282-cpu/), [vLLM PR #5584](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/5584)). **Survey artifact:** `survey/alternative-stacks.md` (sar_6XU4Dsb_mvhn).

title: Layered spec + Sarathi-Serve scheduling on single GPU fleet
claimMd: For the default mixed-chat workload (512 prompt / 128 completion), a hosting stack that combines (1) Sarathi-Serve-style stall-free chunked prefill with decode-priority token budgets and (2) per-request layered speculation—suffix/ngram for repetitive prefixes, then MTP or EAGLE when the checkpoint supports it, else plain decode—beats stock vLLM (continuous batching + default chunked-prefill tuning) on cost per token by an ESTIMATE 1.4–2.2× on the same GPU SKU. Mechanism: Sarathi-Serve reports up to 2.6× serving capacity vs vLLM on Mistral-7B (A100); vLLM’s own spec-decode table shows EAGLE/MTP retain medium–high gain at high QPS where draft-model spec fades; n-gram/suffix add throughput without draft VRAM. Combined effect is multiplicative on GPU utilization and inverse effective decode steps, not latency-only.
evidenceMd:
Sarathi-Serve vs vLLM serving capacity: https://www.usenix.org/conference/osdi24/presentation/agrawal (2.6× Mistral-7B, 1×A100).

Sarathi chunked prefill + decode-maximal batching: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.16369

vLLM chunked prefill policy (decode-first): https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.8.1/performance/optimization.html

vLLM speculative method QPS tradeoffs (EAGLE/MTP high at high QPS; draft_model medium): https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/speculative_decoding/

EAGLE 2.7–3.5× latency / 2× throughput on LLaMA2-70B: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.15077

Leviathan acceptance/speedup model (exact distribution): https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.17192v1

Survey artifact: survey/batching-speculative.md. All $/token multipliers ESTIMATE; no local GPU measurements.

title: FP8-resident KV: same-GPU concurrency doubling for chat $/token
claimMd: For monolithic vLLM-like serving on the orchestrator default workload (512 prompt / 128 completion, mixed chat), enabling production FP8 KV cache (--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 with validated attention backend) approximately halves KV bytes per token versus BF16, which directly increases decode-limited batch capacity B on the same GPU SKU. Holding G ($/GPU-hr) fixed, effective $/token scales roughly as 1/B, yielding an ESTIMATE ~1.5–1.9× improvement in tokens per GPU-dollar versus BF16 baseline when serving is KV-memory-bound (typical at moderate concurrency on 7B–70B class models). This beats “more of the same vLLM” without adding tiers, disaggregation, or extra nodes—provided accuracy stays within SLO (vLLM reports near-baseline on validated paths).
evidenceMd:
vLLM FP8 KV blog states memory-bound decode can reduce per-token KV cost to ~54% of BF16 and that KV dominates at 128k+ contexts; recommends FP8 as default starting point: https://vllm-project.github.io/2026/04/22/fp8-kvcache.html

Quantized KV docs describe fp8_e4m3/e5m2 and memory footprint reduction: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/quantization/quantized_kvcache/

PagedAttention establishes that batch/concurrency is KV-capacity limited: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180

KIVI (research upper bound for aggressive quantization) reports 2.6× less peak memory and 2.35–3.47× throughput from batch expansion—shows mechanism, not vLLM production path: https://mlanthology.org/icml/2024/liu2024icml-kivi/

All throughput multipliers labeled ESTIMATE; no GPU measurements in this swarm cycle.

title: Break-even gated cluster KV pool (Mooncake + py-kvcache policy)
claimMd: A hosting topology that keeps vLLM PagedAttention on GPU but adds a shared DRAM/NVMe KV pool (Mooncake/LMCache/vLLM TieringOffloadingSpec pattern) with scheduler-side admission control—load external KV only when prefix_length ≥ workload-specific break-even L*—beats GPU-only vLLM on $/token when (a) prefix token hit rate h is material (shared system prompts, multi-turn, or long reused documents) AND (b) median prompt length exceeds L* where NVMe/DRAM load + H2D transfer is cheaper than GPU prefill. For pure 512-token unique chat on fast GPUs, external tiers often lose (py-kvcache: H100 avg request below break-even); for 8k–128k reused corpora Mooncake reports 59–498% effective capacity gains and Kimi production +75–115% request handling, implying lower $/token via higher useful throughput on existing GPU fleets by trading cheap storage for prefill FLOPs.
evidenceMd:
Mooncake disaggregated KV pool using CPU/DRAM/SSD/RDMA: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.00079 ; FAST'25 operational results 59–498% capacity vs baselines, 115%/107% more requests on A800/H800: https://www.usenix.org/system/files/fast25-qin.pdf

vLLM tiered offload (CPU primary + FS secondary), async DMA, sizing guidance cpu_bytes_to_use > aggregate GPU KV for hit rate: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features/kv_offloading_usage/

py-kvcache: external cache not automatic win; break-even depends on prefix length/GPU; preload moves I/O off critical path; H100 short requests favor GPU recompute: http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11744

LMCache cross-request reuse order GPU→LMCache→recompute: https://docs.lmcache.ai/mp/disaggregated_prefill.html

Cost mechanism: NVMe $/GB << HBM $/GB (ESTIMATE); profitability requires h and L above threshold—label all $/token deltas ESTIMATE until benchmarked.
